explanation: In the United Kingdom, showing the soles of your feet is considered impolite, especially in social settings, as it is associated with disrespect and uncleanliness. This gesture can be interpreted as a sign of contempt or carelessness, particularly if directed at someone. The custom stems from traditional British etiquette that values keeping feet flat on the floor and avoiding pointing feet at others.
local_tip: Keep both feet flat on the floor or crossed at the ankles, and never point the sole of your shoe or foot toward anyone during conversation.

also_check.note: The feet are considered the lowest and dirtiest part of the body; showing soles is deeply offensive.
Generally less offensive but can be seen as casual or rude in formal settings; context matters.
Showing the sole of your foot or shoe is a serious insult, especially in Arab cultures.
